commitA.subject: feat(campaign): refresh the client record after a committed acceptance is acknowledged
commitA.rationale: The mapping statement is correct and pinned by value, the refetch bridge is the right (and smaller) answer, the fence echo is complete on both client write paths and survives a 200 and a 409, and the falsification is genuinely 1:1. Two required edits, both narrow and both on the FAILURE side of the new action: it clears the armed auto-save and never re-arms it (regressing the invariant the crash-window F1 fix in the same file exists to protect), and it is the first refetch-replace call site in the codebase without task 1.3's dirty-state exemption -- which the receipt records as a non-claim but the code does not state at all.

commitB.rationale: Test-only, 57 insertions, no product file touched. Row 6's by-value assertion against both journal numbers is the strongest row in the file and is the one that actually pins the mapping statement. Row 4 correctly proves the refresh never writes and never adopts a version it did not read.

requiredEdits.finding: `refreshAfterCommittedCommandAction` calls `clearAutoSaveTimer()` and NEVER re-arms. On every non-adopting path of `runLoad` -- the network/500 throw (`:953-956`), the 404 adoptable branch (`:894-901`), and the 404 not-found branch (`:902-904`) -- `dirty` is left exactly as it was while the armed save has been cancelled, so a dirty client is left with NO pending write until the player's next mutation, which may never come. This is verbatim the failure mode the crash-window F1 fix names in its own doc block a few lines above (`:1204-1210`: 'nothing else would re-arm the debounce until the next mutation - which may never come, leaving the campaign dirty with no pending write'), and `reconcileAfterDiscardFlushAction` closes it by arming on EVERY path (`:1253-1257`, `.then((adopted) => { armAutoSaveTimer(set, get); return adopted; })`). The new action's own inline comment at `:1309` -- 'This refresh owns the next write' -- is true on the adopting path and false on all three others. Test row 4 does not catch it because it calls `markDirty()` after the failed refresh, which re-arms the timer itself (`:1341-1345`).
requiredEdits.minimalFix: Mirror the sibling: `const refresh = runLoad(set, campaignId).then((adopted) => { if (!adopted && get().dirty) { armAutoSaveTimer(set, get); } return adopted; });` (or arm unconditionally as `reconcileAfterDiscardFlushAction` does -- `armAutoSaveTimer` already clears before re-arming and the timer body returns early on `saveState === 'conflict'`, `:1070-1072`).
requiredEdits.testObligation: One row: a DIRTY client whose acknowledgement refetch does not answer still has a pending write -- advance `AUTO_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS` with NO intervening `markDirty()` and assert a PUT was issued at the pre-command token. That row is red against the committed code.

requiredEdits.finding: The dirty-client case is described in the receipt as 'inherited from 1.3', but that is only half true and the code says nothing at all. Task 1.3's replace-not-merge law is safe BECAUSE unsaved work is exempted at the CALL SITE -- 1.3's own receipt says so ('Unsaved work is protected by the dirty-state exemption at the call site, which is a fact about the SESSION, not a claim about the cache') and the only existing refetch-replace call site implements it (`src/pages-modules/gameplay/campaigns/campaignPageShell.tsx:151-156`, `cacheNeedsValidation = routeMatches && !dirty && ...`, with the comment 'Dirty local state is exempt (the save path's conflict handling reconciles it)'). `refreshAfterCommittedCommand` is a NEW `runLoad` call site with no `!dirty` exemption AND it cancels the armed save, i.e. it removes the very conflict handling that comment defers to. A reader of this function cannot learn from it that an acknowledgement arriving while the client is dirty silently discards the unsaved mutations (`runLoad` replaces the campaign whole on a diverged key `:930-941` and sets `dirty: false` `:944`). The doc block's affirmative list of what it does not do ('never writes, never adopts a version it did not read, never treats either journal number as a row version') reads as exhaustive and is not.
requiredEdits.minimalFix: Add one paragraph to the doc block stating that this is the one refetch-replace call site without task 1.3's dirty-state exemption, that an acknowledgement arriving while the client is dirty discards the unsaved local mutations whole, and that closing it is 6.2b's (its client half is required to obtain an acknowledged save before submitting the command).
requiredEdits.explicitNonDemand: Do NOT add the `!dirty` guard as part of this edit. Skipping the refresh while dirty would trade the lost edit for an unexplained 409 on the next save; that is a design decision belonging to 6.2b, not to this review.

interleaving_ackDuringInFlightSave.verdict: SAFE FOR THE SERVER, LOSSY FOR THE CLIENT -- non-blocking, recorded
interleaving_ackDuringInFlightSave.analysis: `refreshAfterCommittedCommand` does not await an in-flight SAVE (the store has no `inFlightSave`; `runSave`'s only wait is on `inFlightLoad`, `:789-791`). So a PUT already past that guard races the refresh. If the source moved the row, that PUT is refused -- by the CAS, or ahead of it by 6.1's fence guard (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:145-153 on the 6.1 branch) -- and `runSave` sets `saveState: 'conflict'` (`:834-838`). The refresh then resolves and `runLoad` overwrites that with `saveState: 'saved'` and `conflictServerRecord: null` (`:942-951`). Net: the client ends holding the SERVER's record at the server's version, so nothing incorrect is ever written to the server; but a conflict the player was shown is cleared without explanation and any local edit is replaced whole. Acceptable for an action with no production caller, but it is the second face of RE-A2 and 6.2b's caller must not assume the two paths are ordered.

interleaving_ackWhileDirty.isItSafe: Safe in the sense the brief asks: it is never a silent overwrite of the server. The refresh only READS; the only write that follows is an ordinary PUT at a token the client actually read. It is NOT safe for local work: `runLoad` replaces the campaign whole (`:930-941`) and clears `dirty` (`:944`), so unsaved mutations are discarded with no toast, no `flushSkip`, and no other surfaced signal.
interleaving_ackWhileDirty.inheritedOrNew: The REPLACEMENT is inherited from 1.3. The EXPOSURE is new: 1.3's protection for unsaved work is the call-site `!dirty` exemption (campaignPageShell.tsx:151-156), and this is the first `runLoad` call site that omits it while also cancelling the save path that exemption defers to.

3_fenceEcho.heldFromEveryReadRecord: PASS -- `sourceReplayFence: fenceOf(record)` is set at all four record-adopting sites: `applySavedRecord` (:727), `rollbackCoopCampaign` (:751), `runLoad` (:949), `resolveConflictTakeServer` (:1377). `fenceOf` (:553-557) normalizes `undefined` to `null`.
3_fenceEcho.echoedOnBothClientWritePaths: PASS -- the ordinary save (`putLiveCampaign` :663-670, fed `get().sourceReplayFence` from `runSave` :809-813) and the discard-time keepalive flush (`flushPendingMutationsAction` :1108-1119, fed `state.sourceReplayFence`). Every non-test `buildSerializedCampaign` call site and every non-test `method: 'PUT'` in the client was enumerated: the only two that hit `/api/campaigns/[id]` are these two and both are wrapped. `runAdoptLegacyCampaign` (:990) builds an unfenced envelope, which is correct -- it POSTs `/adopt`, which reaches `saveCampaign(envelope, 0)` for a row that does not exist, so `storedFence` is `null` and the guard does not fire (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:144-153 on the 6.1 branch).
3_fenceEcho.neverMintsOrAdvances: PASS -- `withSourceReplayFence` (:566-571) returns the envelope unchanged when the held fence is `null` (conditional spread, never an enumerable `undefined`), so an unfenced campaign sends byte-identically to pre-field behaviour. No arithmetic on `rootPublicRevision` exists anywhere in the client.
3_fenceEcho.doesTheEchoSurviveApplySavedRecordAfterA: PASS, AND VERIFIED CROSS-BRANCH. This was the one place the echo could have died silently. On the 6.1 branch the 200 body is `stored`, built as `{ ...withoutClientFence(prepared.record), version: nextVersion, ...(storedFence === null ? {} : { sourceReplayFence: storedFence }) }` (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:160-166) -- the server strips the CLIENT's fence and re-stamps the STORED one, so the acknowledged record carries it and `applySavedRecord` -> `fenceOf(record)` retains it. The client-side migration is transparent to the field: `migrateClientRecord` -> `migrateSerializedCampaign` returns the snapshot unchanged once it is at the current schema version (campaignMigration.ts:105-128), so nothing field-picks the fence away.
3_fenceEcho.behaviourOnThe409: PASS -- never an overwrite. The 6.1 guard answers a missing/altered fence with `conflictFromStoredRow` (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:150-153), i.e. the SAME typed 409 carrying the current record (`:446-465`, which spreads through `hydrateCampaignRecord` -> `{ ...migrated, ... }` so the stored fence reaches the body). Client-side that lands in `readConflictBody` -> `status: 'conflict'` -> `saveState: 'conflict'` with ONE attempt and no re-PUT (`:678-682`, `:822-838`); `resolveConflictTakeServer` then adopts the server record INCLUDING its fence (`:1377`), and for co-op `rollbackCoopCampaign` does the same (`:751`). So a fence refusal is recoverable through the existing conflict path and can never become a blind overwrite.
3_fenceEcho.flushDigestUnaffected: PASS, verified independently of the receipt: `flushedEnvelopeDigest` (:366-376) hashes schemaVersion / campaignId / savedAt / originDeviceId / body only. The fence is outside the digest, so the post-flush `adoptFlushedRevision` comparison (:1183-1189) is unaffected by the server stripping and re-stamping it. Crash-window suite re-run green (see measuredRuns).
3_fenceEcho.residualNote: `adoptFlushedRevision` reaches `applySavedRecord(set, record)` (:1190) with the READ-BACK record, so it adopts the fence too. Correct, and it is the only other path that could have gone stale.

RE_A1_guardedVsUnconditional.verdict: SAFE -- the guard is the correct choice, not a shortcut
RE_A1_guardedVsUnconditional.canTheGuardLeaveADirtyClientWithoutAWrit: NO, on every path `runLoad` can take. `runLoad` sets `dirty: false` ONLY on the branch that returns true (the 200 adopt path); all three false-returning exits (the catch at :953-956, the 404-adoptable branch at :894-901, the 404-not-found branch at :902-904) leave `dirty` untouched, so `!adopted && get().dirty` is exactly the set of paths where a write is still owed. There is no path where `adopted === true` and a write is still owed for work the refresh did not replace or clear.
RE_A1_guardedVsUnconditional.whyUnconditionalWouldBeWrongHere: Confirmed by reading rather than taken on trust: `performSave` (:770-780) chains straight into `runSave`, and `runSave` does NOT consult `dirty` (:782-861) -- it saves whatever the live campaign holds.
